Create test items

Create a small item family, purchased components and one manufactured item, ready for a production order.

Module
Common, Procurement, Manufacturing, Warehousing

Before you start

  • An existing work center and an existing reference operation for the site. This task does not create work centers, machines, or reference operations. Look them up first — Manufacturing ➔ Job Shop ➔ Shop Layout ➔ Work Centers tirou0101m000 and Manufacturing ➔ Job Shop ➔ Shop Layout ➔ Reference Operations tirou4150m000 — and if neither has a usable entry for the site, stop and obtain one.

Procedure

1Confirm the test design

Result
Site, warehouses, units, and unused item codes are known.
Screen
Warehousing➔Master Data➔Warehouses➔Warehouses whwmd2500m000

Why LN works this way. Nothing yet. Every later task reads a value recorded here, and the one that bites is the warehouse type: a Shop Floor warehouse cannot be received into as a Normal one can, and a description does not say which it is. Where every physical item is of type Product, as on the walked run, buying or making is a supply-source decision rather than an item-type one.

1.1Confirm the approved training companyWrite downtraining company
1.2Select the site that will buy, store, make, and sell the test familyWrite downsite
1.3Open Warehouses whwmd2500m000The warehouse master list opens
1.4Filter the warehouse list to the site from step 1.2Only candidate warehouses for that site remain
1.5Record the approved Normal warehouse for purchased production materialsWrite downpurchased-item warehouse
1.6Record the approved Normal warehouse for finished productsWrite downfinished-item warehouse
1.7Open one approved physical Product item that uses the same counting basisIts global item data opens
1.8Record its Unit SetWrite downUnit Set
1.9Record its Inventory UnitWrite downInventory Unit
1.10Search Items for each proposed example codeNo existing item uses any proposed code

A candidate “raw material” warehouse is Shop FloorSelect an approved Normal warehouse; do not rely on description alone

2Create two item groups

Result
Purchase and Job Shop defaults remain isolated from each other.
Screen
Master Data➔Items➔Item Classification➔Item Groups tcmcs0123m000

Why LN works this way. Item Defaults is keyed by item type and item group, so the group is the handle every default hangs on. Two groups exist because the two roles need different supply sources, and a group is nothing more than a code, a description and a currency until Configure the purchased group attaches defaults to it.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Search for the proposed purchased-group codeNo existing row uses it
2.2Select NewA blank item-group row opens
2.3Enter Item Group and Description for the purchased groupWrite downpurchased-supply item group
2.4Set Currency to the approved company currencyThe currency is populated
2.5Save the purchased groupThe purchased group is available for defaults
2.6Repeat steps 2.1–2.5 for the made groupWrite downmade-supply item groupboth dedicated groups are available for defaults

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Either item-group code already existsUse new dedicated group codes rather than changing an existing group

3Configure the purchased group

Result
BAM-RM can create Ordering, Purchase, and Warehousing data.
Screen
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults tcibd0102m000

Why LN works this way. A default combination records, per package, two separate things: whether default data exists for the subentity, shown by the indicator, and whether a new item should receive it, set by the Create check box. A green indicator with the box cleared gives a new item nothing. The Sites check box decides whether new items get a site row automatically.

4Configure the made group

Result
BAM-FG can create Ordering, Production, Warehousing, and Sales data.
Screen
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Defaults tcibd0102m000

Why LN works this way. The same mechanism as Configure the purchased group with a different supply source and two more packages. Job Shop names manufacture at a production facility as the default source and creates nothing else, and the Production defaults session only opens when Job Shop by Site is active. A Sales default change offers to propagate to existing items, which for an isolated new group is declined.

Warning
The values in the family sheet combine an approved Product/Job Shop reference, the existing M010 finished-goods defaults, and the company's reference currency. Do not reuse them in another company without repeating those checks.

4.4On the site row, set Supply Source to Job ShopWrite downmade default supply sourcethe Product/BAM-FG combination exists with its site row
4.5Repeat for Ordering and Warehousing. Follow steps 3.16–3.21
4.6Compare each with an approved finished Product/Job Shop referenceBoth indicators active, both Create boxes selected, no unapproved planning value introduced

4.8Compare every visible field with the family sheet. Its made-group Production values are in §4

4.10Confirm the Production indicator is active and select the Create check box beside ProductionNew items are marked to receive Production data
4.11Open the blue Sales linkItem - Sales Defaults tdisa0102s000 opens
4.12Complete the Ordering, Price and Delivery tabs from the family sheet. Its made-group Sales values are in §4
4.13Select OKThe Sales defaults are saved

5Verify site creation control

Result
Site-level creation agrees with the company defaults.
Screen
Master Data➔Items➔Defaults➔Item Control and Defaults by Site tcibd1552m000

Why LN works this way. The Create controls can be governed at the site instead of the company. When Centrally Managed is selected the site mirrors the company defaults and the controls are disabled here; when it is cleared the site's own controls decide, and an item created before this is checked can arrive with fewer subentities than its group promised, with no message naming the cause.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Open the row for the site, Product and the purchased group. The site is from step 1.2, and the group from step 2.3The purchased site-control row opens
5.2Read Centrally ManagedThe source of the Create controls is visible
5.3If centrally managed, check the subentities are disabled locally. Ordering, Purchase and Warehousing mirror Configure the purchased group
5.4If not, select them and saveThe purchased site is marked to create those subentities
5.5Repeat steps 5.1–5.4 for the made group. Use Ordering, Production, Warehousing and Sales; the made group is the one from step 2.6The made site is marked to create those subentities

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Site Create controls are disabledRead Centrally Managed; when selected, correct the governing tcibd0502m000 control instead of the site row

6Create the three items

Result
Each item inherits its group's defaults and its site row shows the intended role.
Screen
Master Data➔Items➔Items tcibd0501m000

Why LN works this way. On save, LN gives the new item the supply source, units and subentities its group's defaults promised and, if the Sites box was set, a site row. The saved site row is where the promise is checked: the supply source and the indicators on it prove Configure the purchased group to Verify site creation control, which is why nothing inheritable is typed here.

Note
Create the two purchased items first and the pair last, and do not create the pair until Configure the made group has approved Production and Sales defaults.
Note
The Item identifier has separate Project and Item portions. These are standard test items: leave Project blank and enter the BAM-* code in the Item portion. If General Projects tcmcs0152s000 opens from the Project lookup, close it without creating a project.

6.1Open Items tcibd0501m000The global item overview opens
6.2Select NewA blank Item record opens

6.4Set Item Type to Product and Item Group to the item's group from Create two item groupsSupply source, Unit Set, and Inventory Unit default from Configure the purchased group or 3
6.5Complete any remaining field the screen marks required, using the family valuesWrite downitem Grade, if the screen requires one
6.6Save the item header before working in the Sites gridThe item header is saved
6.7In the Sites grid, ignore the editable filter row marked with =. If no saved row begins with the site from step 1.2, run Create Items by Site from the tab's appropriate menu; if that produces nothing, select New on the Sites toolbar, select that site, and save the recordA saved site line beginning with the actual site code exists
6.8Select the saved site line and open it with the row-arrow buttonItems by Site opens for this item and site
6.9Verify Default Supply Source matches the item's role — Purchase for the rod and the sleeve, Job Shop for the pairWrite downsite supply source
6.10Verify the site subentity indicators — Ordering, Purchase, and Warehousing for a purchased item; Ordering, Production, Warehousing, and Sales for the pairWrite downsite subentities
6.11Repeat steps 6.2–6.10 for the remaining items, each with its own groupAll three items and their site rows match the family sheet §1

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
The item code is rejectedFollow the current item-code segmentation; do not modify segmentation for the experiment

7Build the job shop bill of material

Result
The pair has an Approved BOM carrying both components.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Bills of Material tibom3100m000

Why LN works this way. A bill of material is written against the item, per site, and cannot be used for manufacture until its revision is approved; approval and the two use indicators, for planning and for costing, are three separate actions. The material lines carry the issuing warehouse, and the revision's effective date decides whether a production order's reference date selects it.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Open Job Shop Bills of Material tibom3100m000The BOM overview opens for one site
7.2Confirm Site is the site from step 1.2Only that site's bills of material are listed
7.3Filter Product for the finished item from Create the three itemsNo bill of material exists yet for the chopstick pair
7.4Select NewA blank BOM header opens
7.5Set Product to the finished itemBAM-CHOP-PAIR is selected
7.6Set BOM Quantity to 1The material quantities below are the quantities for one pair
7.7Set Effective Date on or before the date of the production order you intend to runThe revision will be valid on that order's reference date
7.8Leave Routing blankThe BOM stays usable with any routing
7.9Save the headerWrite downBOM and revision; Status = New
7.10Open the saved BOM and go to its material linesJob Shop List of Materials tibom3110m000 opens for this BOM and revision

7.12Add a line: Item = the paper sleeve, Net Quantity = 1One sleeve per pair
7.13On both lines, set Warehouse to the raw-material warehouse. It is the one from step 1.5Each material will be issued from the warehouse Stock the components stocks
7.14Leave Scrap Percentage and Scrap Quantity at zeroNo material loss is modelled in this test
7.15Save the material linesWrite downBOM materials storedboth lines belong to this BOM revision
7.16Select the BOM row and run Actions➔Approve RevisionStatus = Approved; Approved By and Approved On are filled
7.17With the same row selected, run Actions➔Use for Planning IndicatorUse for Planning is selected on the row
7.18With the same row selected, run Actions➔Use for Costing IndicatorUse for Costing is selected on the row
7.19Close and reopen the BOMWrite downBOM approved and in useApproved, both indicators set, both material lines present

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do

The BOM stays at NewOnly Approved bills of material can be used for manufacture. Run Actions➔Approve Revision on the selected row
Use for Planning is refusedAnother BOM already holds it for this item and site — one per item and site for planning, one per product for costing

8Build the job shop routing

Result
The pair has an Approved routing with an operation at a work center.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Engineering➔Job Shop Routings tirou4100m000

Why LN works this way. The routing gives the production order operations to report complete; without one there are no estimated production costs and nothing triggers the finished-goods receipt. A reference operation is a template that carries its own times into the operation line, and the routing quantity is what makes those times the times for one pair.

StepActionYou should see
8.1Open Job Shop Routings tirou4100m000The routing overview opens
8.2Confirm Site is the site from step 1.2Only that site's routings are listed

8.5Set Product to the finished itemBAM-CHOP-PAIR is selected

8.7Set Effective Date on or before the date of the production order you intend to runThe revision will be valid on that order's reference date
8.8Set Routing Quantity to 1Operation times entered below are the times for one pair
8.9Retain the proposed Minimum Quantity and Maximum QuantityThe routing is not restricted to a quantity band the test did not choose
8.10Leave Calculate and the lead-time fields at their proposed valuesNo invented lead time enters the test data
8.11On the Operations grid, select NewA blank operation line opens
8.12Enter Operation = 10The pair has a first operation
8.13Set Reference Operation and Work Center to existing values from the prerequisite lookupsWrite downrouting operation and work center
8.14Check what the reference operation brought with itA reference operation carries its own times; do not overwrite them with an invented value
8.15Enter Cycle Time (min) only if it is still blank
8.16Confirm Production Rate is filled. Where Use Production Rates is selected in the current parameter set, that is the value LN uses for the operation timeThe production rate is expressed per hour here
8.17Save the operation lineThe operation is stored against the routing revision
8.18Select the routing and approve the revision from the Actions menuStatus = Approved; Approved By and Approved On are filled
8.19Set Use for Planning on the routingUse for Planning is selected
8.20Set Use for Costing on the routingUse for Costing is selected
8.21Close and reopen the routingWrite downrouting and revisionApproved, indicators set, operation present

9Confirm costing data

Result
Every item in the family carries the standard cost the estimate calculation reads.
Screen
Common➔Standard Costs➔Master Data➔Item - Costing ticpr0107m000

Why LN works this way. A production order's estimate reads each material's standard cost, and a parameter decides whether a missing one stops the calculation or silently lowers it. Purchased items get their standard cost from purchase price data, so the two components will have none until Stock the components buys them in.

StepActionYou should see
9.1Open Item - Costing ticpr0107m000 for the bamboo rodThe item's costing record opens for an enterprise unit
9.2Read Costing Source, then on the Standard Cost tab Material Costs and Total CostsWrite downcomponent standard coststhe rod's figures
9.3Repeat for the paper sleeveWrite downcomponent standard coststhe sleeve's figures
9.4Open the record for the finished itemWrite downfinished-item standard cost
9.5Open Item Standard Costs ticpr3501m000 for each item whose cost is missing or unexpected. Use the item's effective dateThe actual and historical standard cost structure is shown, or confirms none exists
9.6If an item still has no standard cost, stop. Obtain the approved cost route before continuingThe estimate calculation is not left to run against missing material costs

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
A purchased component has no standard costIts standard cost is calculated from purchase price priority levels; the item needs purchase price data before it will have one

10Stock the components

Result
The rod and sleeve are on hand at the raw-material warehouse.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000

Why LN works this way. A production order can be created and released with no stock, but it cannot be finished, because the material issue has nothing to issue. Buying the components in exercises the Purchase defaults and creates the purchase price history their standard cost is calculated from; the inventory figure at the raw-material warehouse, not the receipt status, is the proof.

10.1Open Inventory 360 and filter for the bamboo rodThe rod appears with inventory totals
10.2Click Warehouse Inventory
10.3Read the raw-material warehouse. It is the one from step 1.5Write downrod on hand before, expected to be 0 for a new item
10.4Repeat steps 10.1–10.3 for the paper sleeveWrite downsleeve on hand beforeboth baselines recorded before anything is booked
10.5Create a purchase order in Purchase Order Intake Workbench tdpur4601m200Purchase Order tdpur4100m900 opensWrite downcomponent stocking route used
10.6Open the lookup on Buy-from Business Partner. It is Buy-from Business Partners tccom4520m000The partner list opens
10.7Select the partnerOne run used one of the standard test partners
10.8Set Order Type, Purchase Office and Ship-toThe order takes a number. One run showed Order Type IPO (Inventory Purchase Order), the partner's purchase office and the site as ship-to
10.9Book the order lines from the BOM, not from habitOne line per component. One run booked line 10 BAM-ROD qty 2.0000 ea and line 20 BAM-SLEEVE qty 1.0000 ea, both to the raw-materials warehouse
10.10On the generated Warehousing Order whinh2100m100, run Actions➔Receive on the inbound linesOrder Type PUI "Purchase Receipts", ship-from the business partner, ship-to the raw-materials warehouse
10.11Confirm the Warehouse Receipt whinh3512m000Status = Confirmed, All Lines Final and All Lines Complete both set
10.12Re-read both items in Inventory 360 at the raw-material warehouseWrite downrod on hand after andsleeve on hand aftereach increased by the booked quantity

SymptomWhat to do

11Qualify the training case

Result
The family is qualified to start Production order.

Why LN works this way. Nothing new. This task checks the family against what Production order's Confirm the existing foundation asks for and hands the values over. The boundary is here because a fact lives in one file, and the order itself belongs to Production order.

This task creates nothing. It checks the family against what Production order asks for in its Confirm the existing foundation, and hands over.

StepActionYou should see
11.1Confirm all three items and their site rows show the right supply sources. They were verified at step 6.9The family is intact
11.2Open the BOM from step 7.19
11.3Confirm it is Approved and used for planning and costing
11.4Confirm it carries both materialsThe pair has a manufacturable structure
11.5Open the routing from step 8.21
11.6Confirm it is Approved and used for planning and costing
11.7Confirm it carries its operation and work centerThe pair has something to report complete
11.8Confirm both components are on hand at the raw-material warehouse. It is the one from step 10.12There is material to issue
11.9Confirm the pair should be received into the finished-item warehouse. It is the one from step 1.6The receiving warehouse is a decision, not a discovery made mid-order
11.10Confirm the costing figures from steps 9.2–9.4 are still presentThe estimate calculation has what it reads
11.11Take the values from steps 11.1–11.10 to Production order
11.12Run Production order with themWrite downtraining case qualified

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
The production order opens with no BOM or routingCompare the order's reference date with the effective dates from step 7.7 and step 8.7. A revision effective after the reference date is not selected
The production order has no operation to report completeRecheck Build the job shop routing — an approved routing with at least one operation is what Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt reports against

Variations

CaseWhat changes
Minimum two-item testCreate only one purchased material and one Job Shop finished product. This proves the two supply patterns but gives the later BOM only one material class
Recommended three-item testUse this whole process: two purchased inputs and one Job Shop finished product
Four-item multilevel testAdd a semi-finished level only after the single-level case works; it requires another made-item master, BOM, routing, and costing layer, and a second production order
Purchased finished goodsUse another dedicated Product group with Default Supply Source = Purchase; no Job Shop Production defaults are required, and Build the job shop bill of material and Build the job shop routing do not apply
Items only
Task 6		Stop after this task. The family exists as master data but cannot be produced; Build the job shop bill of material to Qualify the training case are what make it runnable
Production quantity greater than one
Task 10		Book proportionally more component stock in this task — 2 rods and 1 sleeve per pair. The steps do not change
